comment: Pins the SDK feature band (10.0.1xx) so the CI format gate is reproducible.
ci.yml runs `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` with the style AND analyzer passes. Those
passes are implemented by the SDK's bundled analyzers, so a new SDK can turn that gate red on
a PR that changed nothing relevant. Without a pin, `dotnet-version: 10.x` in ci.yml means the
SDK can change under us at any time.
rollForward is `latestPatch`, NOT `latestFeature`. latestPatch stays inside the 10.0.1xx
feature band and takes servicing patches only; latestFeature would allow 10.0.2xx, and new or
retuned analyzers ship in feature bands. latestFeature would therefore reintroduce the exact
drift this file exists to prevent. Issue #62 said latestFeature; that was wrong for the stated
Bumping the feature band is a deliberate act: change `version` here, run `dotnet format`, and
commit any resulting changes with the bump.
testComment: Selects Microsoft.Testing.Platform as the runner for `dotnet test` (#70). This is the opt-in
the 10.0.1xx SDK looks for; `dotnet test -h` names global.json explicitly, and the
[dotnet.test.runner] section of a root dotnet.config - which the preview documentation
described - is NOT read by this band. If it were ever honoured instead, this key would still
win, so leave it here rather than moving it.
It is required, not a preference. The test project references xunit.v3 and no VSTest adapter,
so without this `dotnet test` routes to VSTest and Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild.targets
fails the build outright with 'Testing with VSTest target is no longer supported'. That is a
loud failure rather than a silent zero-test pass, which is the one piece of luck in this
migration - but it does mean this key and the xunit.v3 reference have to move together.
It also puts the runner choice in the same file as the SDK pin, so the two facts that decide
how CI runs tests are read together.
